Where to Stay in Tak?

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Tak hotels across every budget — a new boutique in Mae Sot, a Ping River room in Tak town, a riverside resort that bases you for the Thee Lor Su waterfall in Umphang, and a city hotel from ฿450/night. Covering the three key areas: riverside Tak town, border-town Mae Sot, and Umphang for Thee Lor Su. From roughly ฿450–1,300/night.
heroStats: 🗺️ 3 key areas (Tak Town·Mae Sot·Umphang–Thee Lor Su)
introH2: 🗺️ Why does choosing the right area in Tak matter so much?
introHtml: Tak is a big province with its main draws spread across different districts, so where you stay really does shape the trip. Riverside Tak town (the Chom Phon–Mahat Thai Bamrung district) is the hub for stays, restaurants and the evening market — ideal for exploring the town, sleeping with a river view, or stopping over on a drive north. Mae Sot district, about 80 km from Tak town, is the Thai–Myanmar border town with the most — and newest — hotels in the province, best for cross-border errands, the Rim Moei market, or as a launch point for Umphang. And Umphang district is the farthest out, about 150 km from Mae Sot along the famously winding 1,219-bend road, but it's the gateway to Thee Lor Su, Thailand's largest waterfall — best if nature and rafting are your main goal. Many people book in Tak town hoping for an easy day trip to Thee Lor Su and end up driving all day. This guide rounds up 12 Tak hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Tak has no metro and no train, so you get around by car, and the province is spread out enough that your choice of area sets up the whole trip. Stays in Tak town are the easiest, within walking distance of the Ping River, the evening market and restaurants, with some right on the riverbank. Mae Sot stays sit mostly along the Asian Highway and in the town centre, near markets, the border crossing and Mae Sot Airport, with decent dining around them — but most still need a car. Almost everything in Umphang district needs a private car or an organised tour, as it's far out along a winding road; many stays there bundle Thee Lor Su rafting and trekking packages with a guide. The areas in this guide: Tak Town — riverside, town sightseeing, road-trip stopovers · Mae Sot — border, Rim Moei market, airport · Umphang — base for the Thee Lor Su waterfall and rafting.

entries.name: The Teak Hotel (Mae Sot)
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.2 · 91 reviews · TripAdvisor #3 of 19 hotels in Mae Sot
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Prasat Withi Rd · central Mae Sot · ~10 min to Rim Moei market
tags: 🌿 New boutique with warm teak décor
📍 Central Mae Sot, easy walk to food
entries.addr: 888 Prasat Withi Rd, Mae Sot, Mae Sot District, Tak
entries.storyHtml: The Teak Hotel is the best pick in this guide if you want a new, clean, nicely styled room in Tak — a new boutique in central Mae Sot scoring 9.1 and ranked #3 of 19 hotels in Mae Sot on TripAdvisor. Its 115 rooms have a modern teak-toned look, plus an outdoor pool, fitness room and on-site restaurant. Real guest reviews praise the new, clean, quiet rooms and a breakfast buffet that's more varied than you'd expect in a border town — American and Asian dishes, made-to-order eggs, hot soy milk and steamed buns. The trade-offs: the pool is fairly shaded and cool at times, parking is limited when full, and some balconies are sealed under local rules. Best for staying in Mae Sot town, cross-border errands, or as a stopover before Umphang.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Don't skip breakfast — come early for the freshest spread before the crowds. If you're a light sleeper, ask for a higher floor or a room off the road. To actually use the pool, go late morning to afternoon when the sun warms the water.

Score 9.1 · TripAdvisor #3 of 19 hotels in Mae Sot
Varied breakfast buffet — the most-praised in reviews
Pool, fitness, free parking, central location

entries.name: Viang Tak Riverside Hotel
entries.revCount: Agoda 8.5 · 1,595 reviews (most in this guide) · Trip.com ~9.0
entries.badge: 🌊 On the Ping River · most reviews
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chom Phon Rd · on the Ping River · central Tak town
tags: 🌊 River-view rooms over the Ping + the Rattanakosin Bridge
🚶 Walk to the riverside market & Loi Krathong Sai site
entries.addr: 236 Chom Phon Rd, Rahaeng, Mueang Tak, Tak
entries.storyHtml: Viang Tak Riverside Hotel is the most-reviewed hotel in this guide — over 1,595 reviews — and the riverside name in central Tak town that travellers mention most, scoring around 8.7. Upper-floor river-side rooms look straight out over the Ping River and the 200-year Rattanakosin Bicentennial Bridge, and the nice part is that a river view costs barely more than a city view. Real guest reviews praise the roomy rooms, soft beds, good service, an on-site pool and loaner bikes, plus a few minutes' walk to the riverside market and the Loi Krathong Sai festival site. The catch: the hotel is older and showing its age — some rooms have old carpet, a few amenities are missing, and the karaoke/bar can be noisy some nights. Best for a riverside view in the city centre on a budget, and for road-trip stopovers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a River View room on floor 6 or higher for the full view and distance from the bar noise. Come at year-end for the Loi Krathong Sai festival of a thousand floating lanterns on the Ping River, an easy walk away — rooms fill fast then, so book ahead.
pros: Most reviews in this guide — 1,595 — so plenty of data
River-view rooms over the Ping + the Bicentennial Bridge, barely pricier than city view
Riverside, central location, walk to the riverside market and Loi Krathong Sai site
Pool, kids' pool, free parking and loaner bikes
cons: Older hotel; some rooms dated, old carpet, a few amenities missing
Karaoke/bar noisy some nights — ask for a room away from that zone

entries.name: Hop Inn Mae Sot
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Asian Highway · Mae Sot · near Mae Sot Airport
entries.addr: 81/9 Asian Highway, Mae Sot, Mae Sot District, Tak
entries.storyHtml: Hop Inn Mae Sot takes the top score in this guide at 9.2 — a budget chain whose whole pitch is a clean, comfortable, safe room at a predictable price, with a standout 9.7 cleanliness score from 125 reviews. It's on the Asian Highway near Mae Sot Airport with free parking, handy if you drive in or fly in. Real guest reviews praise the consistently clean, same-everywhere rooms — no surprises. Just know it's pure budget: rooms are small at about 20 sqm and plain, there's no pool or gym, and the soundproofing is only so-so. Best for budget travellers who care about a clean room and value over facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Rooms don't include breakfast — pick the Standard Double + breakfast package at about ฿850, or just walk out for food in Mae Sot town. Book ahead in peak season; it's a popular chain with steady rates.
pros: Top score in this guide — 9.2 · cleanliness 9.7
Consistent chain standard everywhere — no surprises
Affordable, predictable rates · free parking, free Wi-Fi
Near Mae Sot Airport — handy if you drive or fly in
cons: Small ~20 sqm plain rooms, no pool or gym
Only so-so soundproofing · breakfast not in the base rate

entries.name: Centara Life Hotel Mae Sot
entries.revCount: Agoda 8.4 · 436 reviews · the biggest chain hotel in Mae Sot
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Asian Highway · Mae Sot · near Rim Moei market

entries.addr: 100 Inthakhiri Rd Soi 5 (Asian Highway), Mae Sot District, Tak
entries.storyHtml: Centara Life Hotel Mae Sot is the only 4-star in this guide and the most complete chain hotel in Mae Sot, scoring 8.4 from 436 reviews. It's a rare option in a border town because it has a pool, tennis court, fitness room, spacious rooms and big-chain service. Real guest reviews praise the space, full facilities and good service — ideal for families and anyone wanting a 4-star standard in Mae Sot. The trade-offs: the building and rooms look a bit dated, the lift is slow, and on-site food costs more than restaurants outside. Best for families, business travellers, and anyone who values full facilities over newness.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Make the most of the pool, tennis court and fitness room if you stay a few nights. On-site dining is pricier than outside — drive out for cheaper, more varied food in Mae Sot town. Ask for a more recently renovated room when booking.
pros: The only 4-star here, the biggest chain in Mae Sot
Pool, tennis court, fitness, spacious rooms — most complete in town
4-star service, good for families and business trips
Free parking · 436 reviews, plenty of data
cons: Building and rooms look a bit dated, slow lift

entries.name: White House Hotel Tak
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mai Ngam · Mueang Tak · ~3 km from town
entries.addr: 333/3 Moo 7, Mai Ngam, Mueang Tak, Tak
entries.storyHtml: White House Hotel is the budget Tak-town pick whose selling point is having a pool and an open, airy atmosphere, scoring 8.6 from 532 reviews with a high 8.9 cleanliness rating. Opened in 2017, it sits in Mai Ngam sub-district about 3 km from town, a white building set in a wide garden. Real guest reviews praise the clean rooms, soft beds, fresh-looking bedding, a clear pool with a separate kids' pool, plus free loaner bikes and free parking with an EV charger. The trade-off: it's outside town, not walkable to the river or market, so you need a car, and breakfast varies by package so check when booking. Best for families who want the kids in the pool and for people driving through Tak.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a pool-view room — the favourite spot here; with kids, the separate kids' pool is easy. Since it's out of town, plan meals ahead and drive the ~3 km in for food. Use the free bikes for a morning ride.
pros: Outdoor pool + separate kids' pool at a low price
Clean rooms, soft beds, fresh-looking bedding, cleanliness 8.9

cons: ~3 km out of town, not walkable to the river or market — need a car

entries.name: Irawadee Resort (Mae Sot)
entries.addr: 758 Inthakhiri Rd, Mae Sot, Mae Sot District, Tak
entries.storyHtml: Irawadee Resort is the most charming small boutique resort in Mae Sot for travellers who want a warm atmosphere and family-run service, scoring 8.7 from 310 reviews. It's a small 15-room resort in Lanna–Burmese style in central Mae Sot on Inthakhiri Road. Real guest reviews praise the woodwork-rich décor, made-to-order breakfast included in the rate, owner-run care, plus a café, spa and bike rental. The trade-offs: it's a small resort with no pool, some rooms look dated, and it's on the road so there's some traffic noise and roosters in the morning. Best for couples and anyone who values atmosphere and care over a full set of facilities.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The rate includes a made-to-order breakfast — try the much-praised morning menu. Ask for a room off the road if you're worried about traffic and early roosters. With just 15 rooms, book ahead in peak season.
pros: Charming small boutique, attractive Lanna–Burmese woodwork
Made-to-order breakfast included in the rate
Warm, family-run service with a café, spa and bike rental
Central Mae Sot, easy walk to food

entries.name: One Budget Hotel Tak Maesot

entries.addr: 99/242 Asian Highway, Mae Sot, Mae Sot District, Tak
entries.storyHtml: One Budget Hotel Tak Maesot is a budget hotel opened in 2024 whose pitch is new, clean, roomy rooms for a few hundred to low-thousand baht, within walking distance of Robinson, scoring 8.7 from 143 reviews with a Travellers' Choice award. It's on the Asian Highway about 1 km from Robinson mall in Mae Sot. Real guest reviews praise the new-looking, clean, roomy, quiet rooms, a buffet breakfast, plus free parking and free Wi-Fi. Just know it's brand-new: some service still needs polish, you sometimes hear the corridor, and breakfast isn't quite consistent yet. Best for budget travellers who want a new, clean room near the mall in Mae Sot.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a ~1 km walk to Robinson — handy for mall trips and food. Being brand-new, some service is still settling, so flag anything to staff. Kids under 12 eat breakfast free with the family room.

entries.name: Thee Lor Su Riverside Resort (Umphang)
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.0 · 60 reviews · base for Thee Lor Su
entries.badge: 🌊 Base for Thee Lor Su · rafting packages
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On the Mae Klong River · Umphang · base for Thee Lor Su

🚣 Thee Lor Su rafting & trekking packages
🏞️ Base for the Thee Lor Su waterfall
entries.addr: 7 Moo 4, Mae Klong, Umphang District, Tak
entries.storyHtml: Thee Lor Su Riverside Resort is the best riverside resort in this guide for using as a base for the Thee Lor Su waterfall and rafting in Umphang, scoring 9.0 from 60 reviews. Its strength is bundling the stay, fresh-cooked food and a guided tour in one place — riverside cabins on the Mae Klong with balconies over the stream. Real guest reviews praise the riverside setting, tasty fresh-cooked food, and friendly staff and guides. Just know it's a nature stay: rooms are simple, there's no pool, you can't swim in the stream, and the mobile signal can be patchy. Best for travellers focused on Thee Lor Su and Umphang's nature.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Contact the resort about the all-in package — stay, meals, rafting and the Thee Lor Su trek with a guide — and book ahead, especially in the cool season. Thee Lor Su is seasonal, so check the open/closed dates and road conditions before you go. The mobile signal can be patchy, so plan around it.

Riverside cabins on the Mae Klong with balconies, nature setting

The trade-offs: the style is fairly plain and it's an older hotel, there's no pool, breakfast is basic, and it's on a main road so expect some traffic noise. Best for families and road-trippers who want a roomy, low-priced room near town.

entries.name: Silayok Grand Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mahat Thai Bamrung Rd · central Tak town · walk to the Ping River
entries.addr: 315/18 Mahat Thai Bamrung Rd, Rahaeng, Mueang Tak, Tak
entries.storyHtml: Silayok Grand Hotel is the cheapest stay in this guide, from just ฿450, with comfy beds, clean quiet rooms and a central Tak-town location as its pitch, scoring 8.1 from 161 reviews and ranked #2 of 9 hotels in Tak on TripAdvisor. It's a 121-room hotel on Mahat Thai Bamrung Road, within walking distance of the Ping River, the evening market and town restaurants. Real guest reviews praise the soft, comfortable beds, clean quiet rooms, a charming carved-wood lobby, and free parking. The trade-offs: bathrooms are plain with weak shower pressure in some rooms, there's no pool, breakfast is very light, and the entrance is hard to find the first time. Best for people driving through Tak or in town on errands who want a clean, low-priced room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entrance is hard to find the first time — use GPS to navigate in. Check the shower pressure at check-in and ask to switch rooms if it's too weak. Breakfast is very light (just bread and coffee), so plan to grab noodles in town.

entries.storyHtml: Umphangburi Resort is a tidy riverside fit for travellers who come to Umphang for Thee Lor Su and nature but want to stay in Umphang town itself, scoring 8.3 from 62 reviews. It's a riverside cluster of about 19 rooms that's still central, so finding food is easier than at out-of-town stays. Real guest reviews praise the clean cabins, the misty mountain atmosphere, tasty Thai food, and an owner who arranges full Thee Lor Su / rafting tours. Just know the journey to Umphang is long and winding, and it's a remote area, so set expectations on facilities. Best for Thee Lor Su visitors who want to stay in the heart of Umphang town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask the owner about a stay + Thee Lor Su / rafting tour package, priced by group size. Being central in Umphang town, food is easier to find than at out-of-town stays. The drive in is long with 1,219 bends, so allow time and take breaks along the way.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Tak hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in around Tak?
faq.a: It depends on your trip. Riverside Tak town suits town sightseeing, a river-view stay, or a stopover on a drive north (Viang Tak Riverside, Silayok Grand, White House, Suansin Garden). Mae Sot district is the border town with the most — and newest — hotels, best for cross-border errands, the Rim Moei market, or as a base before Umphang (The Teak, Hop Inn, Centara Life, Irawadee, One Budget, B2). Umphang district is the farthest out but it's the gateway to the Thee Lor Su waterfall, best for nature and rafting (Thee Lor Su Riverside, Umphangburi).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Tak hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: budget stays start around ฿450–700/night (Silayok Grand, B2 Mae Sot, Hop Inn, Suansin Garden); mid-range hotels and boutiques run about ฿780–1,000 (One Budget, Viang Tak Riverside, White House, The Teak, Irawadee, Thee Lor Su Riverside); the 4-star and the Umphang resort run about ฿1,200–1,300 (Centara Life, Umphangburi). All are approximate from-rates for standard rooms; rates run higher in festival and cool-season periods, especially for Umphang stays.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to visit the Thee Lor Su waterfall?
faq.a: Thee Lor Su is in Umphang district, far from both Tak town and Mae Sot (about 150 km from Mae Sot along the winding 1,219-bend road). If the waterfall is your main goal, staying in Umphang cuts the drive — Thee Lor Su Riverside Resort ฿1,000, a riverside resort bundling rafting and trekking with a guide, or Umphangburi Resort ฿1,300, riverside in central Umphang town with full tour service from the owner. Thee Lor Su is seasonal, so check the open/closed dates and book ahead in the cool season.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay in Mae Sot?
faq.a: Mae Sot is the border town with the most — and newest — hotels in the province. For a new boutique room, The Teak Hotel ฿900, score 9.1 with a standout breakfast. For a full 4-star, Centara Life Mae Sot ฿1,200 with pool, tennis and fitness. On a budget, Hop Inn ฿700, top score 9.2, or B2 Mae Sot ฿550, the cheapest. For a charming boutique, Irawadee Resort ฿900 in Lanna–Burmese style.

faq.q: ❓ Is Tak easy to get around without a car?
faq.a: Tak has no metro and no train, so without a car, staying in Tak town or central Mae Sot is easiest, with restaurants and markets within walking distance (Silayok Grand, Viang Tak Riverside in Tak town; The Teak, Irawadee in central Mae Sot). Out-of-town stays and almost everything in Umphang district need a private car, a rental, or an organised tour — especially if you're heading to Thee Lor Su.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Tak hotels?
faq.a: Prices differ across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com depending on each site's promotions, so open and compare all three before booking — every review page in this guide includes the comparison links. It can save hundreds of baht a night, especially in the cool season when Thee Lor Su visitors fill Umphang stays fast.
